objectives.text: Work out profit per item from cost and price.
Explain why sellers try to be better or cheaper than other sellers.
Tell a feeling about a company from facts about it.
Treat a mistake as something to learn from.

units.title: Coach Nova's Maker Lab
units.blurb: Run a pretend comet-cookie stand with Coach Nova.

steps.text: Hi, I'm Coach Nova, a made-up guest host! Today we run a pretend comet-cookie stand.
Flour, sugar and a bag cost 40 cents per cookie. That is our only cost.
We sell each cookie for $1. The 60 cents left over is called profit.

steps.q: A cookie costs 40 cents to make, its only cost. It sells for $1. What is the profit?

steps.text: A new stand opens next door. It sells cookies too!
Kids pick the stand with the better cookie, the nicer price or the shorter line.
So stands try to get better, or cheaper. That is good news for kids who buy cookies.

steps.q: Would it help our stand, or hurt it?
steps.why: Better cookies, fair prices and short lines bring kids back.

lessons.title: Being a fan is not a fact

steps.text: I love a rocket-toy company. I'm a big fan!
But loving a company is not a reason to own its shares. Fans can be wrong about the numbers.
Check the facts: Does it make a profit? How did its report cards go? Even good facts are not a promise.
That goes for me too! I'm not telling you to buy anything. Check facts with a grown-up.

steps.q: Your favorite star loves a company. What does that tell you about its shares?
steps.why: Loving a company is a feeling. Facts are what you can check.

steps.text: Once, I put all my pretend coins in one company. Then it had a bad month.
My pretend coins dropped a lot. I felt grumpy, and that is OK.
I learned to spread my coins out. It won't stop every drop, but one company can't sink me.

steps.q: What did Coach Nova learn from her oops?
steps.why: She learned to spread out. Mistakes help us learn.

cost.means: The money you pay to make or get something.
cost.example: One cookie costs 40 cents to make.

fan.means: Someone who really likes a person, team or company.
fan.example: Being a fan is a feeling, not a fact about money.
